axes.brief:
Attlee governed through Parliament, contested elections and accepted defeat.
Focused six-question reassessment: Parliamentary lawmaking and acceptance of electoral defeat frame his government. Post-war administration permitted executive implementation without replacing representative institutions with routine citizen initiatives.
axes.counterEvidence:
Parliamentary sovereignty differs from constitutional judicial review and direct recall.
The owner-defined broader axis includes lawful delegation and direct public control; a lower numerical placement is not a regime classification. Six exact responses and response strengths remain inferred. Retained source access dates are not refreshed unless a source was actually revisited. Unchanged answers and other axes were not re-audited. Parliamentary lawmaking and acceptance of electoral defeat frame his government. Post-war administration permitted executive implementation without replacing representative institutions with routine citizen initiatives.
